content:
arun: quick sync — i'm experimenting with collapsing the loadpath into two orthogonal concerns: (1) index/manifest resolution & verification, (2) transport/hydration. thinking this would simplify safetensors + sharded fallback logic. thoughts?

kate: sounds promising. do you mean a single facade that delegates to IndexResolver + TransportAdapter? :thinking_face: 

arun: exactly. IndexResolver handles checksums, signature verification, manifest-less heuristics. TransportAdapter handles mmap vs http/stream, partial reads, and zero-copy where possible.

mike: main worry is warmup ordering: we still need to express per-shard priority and prefix-kv warm-hints. where does that live?

arun: warm hints become a separate WarmupPolicy component that IndexResolver can emit after resolving which shards are primary/secondary. TransportAdapter consumes the hints to do prioritized reads. keeps responsibilities clear.

julia: love the separation. a few tradeoffs:
- verifying checksums early (index-first) increases latency for first token, but lets us avoid corrupted hotstart failures.
- streaming-verify (verify-as-you-read) reduces startup delay but requires async rollback if verification fails.
Which do we prefer?

arun: proposal: default to index-first for hosted & dedicated (safety), allow streaming-verify opt-in for Private/low-latency edge cases. add a `verify_mode` enum: "index-first", "streaming-verify", "none".

kate: what about partial verification to catch header tampering quickly? maybe verify header + manifest sig first, defer chunk checks to background.

arun: yes — header+manifest early, layer checks async. WarmupPolicy can mark shards "trusted" once header sig matches and then we stream body while background verifies full checksum. fallback to fallback-model if full verify fails.

mike: how do we express atomic handoffs when swapping shard variants (quantized vs full)? need a small swap protocol so inference threads never see mixed layout.

arun: TransportAdapter will expose an atomic swap API: `prepare_swap(new_handle) -> commit_swap()`; underlying mmap or buffer swap performed under a brief lock. plus a checksum of in-memory layout. commit is only visible after commit_swap returns.

julia: ops question: how will telemetry show partial-verified warmstarts? we need signals: warm_hint_applied, partial_verify_pass, partial_verify_fail, commit_swap_latency.

arun: agreed. adding those to loader metrics. ci-bot: note added to eng-ml/loader-metrics checklist :white_check_mark: 

kate: encryption/KMS? Private customers want shard-level encryption. does IndexResolver handle key lookup or TransportAdapter do on-the-fly decrypt?

arun: IndexResolver resolves KMS metadata and hands a decrypt callback to TransportAdapter. TransportAdapter performs streaming decrypt+verify so we never materialize plaintext on disk.

mike: final concern: evictions interacting with warmup. if a shard is evicted mid-stream we need graceful cancellation and re-registration of warm hints.

arun: TransportAdapter will support cancellation tokens and a small eviction callback path that re-enqueues unfinished shards with lower priority. WarmupPolicy keeps idempotent hints.

julia: ok this is coming together. next steps: draft a tiny RFC with interface sketches for IndexResolver, TransportAdapter, WarmupPolicy, and metric names. small POC: implement index-first + async chunk verify for mmap path.

arun: will draft RFC today and ping for review. tagging @kate @mike for followups.

ci-bot: created ticket ML-LOAD-482 in backlog for "loadpath simplification RFC + poc"

arun: thanks — landing this thread for now. :thumbsup:
